**L7809 · A generated file that is also hand-edited drifts silently, and the rebuild restores the wrong value**

**The trap:** a file that is BOTH generated from a template and hand-edited by a session will drift
from its source, and nothing announces it. Measured 2026-10-18 on the Waze sign: the built
`waze-device-sign-letter.html` had been corrected to the new plan copy (8 a month / 150 MB / two
cents) on 2026-10-17 while `templates/v11.tpl.html` still said `$9` and "250 MB included". The build
tool skipped any template without the embedded-font token, so the template that would have restored
the WRONG PRICE on the next rebuild was never the thing anyone looked at. Two copies of the same text,
one right, one wrong, both live.

**How it was found:** strip the difference that the build legitimately injects (the base64 font),
normalise whitespace, then diff template against output. Two copy blocks differed, both in the price
panel. That took one command and should be the first thing done to any generated artefact here.

**The fix, and the general rule:** name the template after the output it emits
(`templates/waze-device-sign-letter.tpl.html` -> `waze-device-sign-letter.html`) so there is exactly
one source and one destination; make the build COPY a template that needs no injection instead of
skipping it (a skip looks like success and leaves the destination stale); and never send a session to
edit a generated file directly -- edit the template, rebuild, then verify the OUTPUT bytes
(`grep -c @font-face` = 0 proved the rebuild actually happened).

**Corollary for proofs:** a PNG proves what a screen shows. For anything that prints, render a PDF and
read `pdfPages`, `/MediaBox` and whether content fits inside the sheet -- one page and a 612x792 box
("8.5 x 11 in") is the only honest evidence a sign prints as one sheet.
